title: Launch notes: Rogue rework, new Warrior and Shaman talents, and a damage pass across every class
summary: Blizzard's last beta notes before launch cover every change since the October 15 update, including the October 28 and 30 hotfixes and the late-October racial pass. All three Rogue trees are reworked around a new Shank ability, Warrior Fury gains Reckless Swings and Improved Whirlwind, Shaman Elemental trades Lava Burst for Call of Thunder and renames Elemental Mastery to Lightning Mastery, the Paladin trees are rebuilt, Feral and Restoration Druid are reshaped, and damage goes up across the classes, with more health for higher level creatures to match.
sourceNote: Blizzard's notes cover everything since the October 15 update, so this entry also covers build 70630 and the October 28 and 30 hotfixes. Entries ending in "Not in Blizzard's notes" are tooltip changes found only in the game data (talentsforever.com's 2026-11-03 pull of client build 70753). Where the notes give a new talent's row but not its column, the planner uses talentsforever's placement and the talent's tooltip says so.
pendingInData: Shaman: Lightning Bolt's higher base damage, and Chain Lightning's higher damage and Mana cost. Only Chain Lightning's 2.5 sec cast time is in the tooltips so far.
Druid: Rip, Rake, Ferocious Bite and Pounce (about 25% more) and Starfire (about 40% more base damage). The tooltips still show the old numbers.
Druid: Bear Form and Dire Bear Form's threat bonus (50% to 115%). Their tooltips don't show threat.

Hunter: Aimed Shot (about 110% more), Arcane Shot (about 30% more, 0.15 Attack Power coefficient), Serpent Sting (about 20% more, 5% Attack Power per tick) and Sniper Shot (100% more). The tooltips still show the old numbers.
Rogue: Deadly Poison and Instant Poison's doubled Attack Power coefficients, and Mutilate's higher flat damage per weapon (Blizzard gives no number).
Shaman: Maelstrom Weapon's doubled chance to trigger. It has no trainer tooltip to check against.

points.text: Developer's notes: "Over the course of Beta, we came to the realization that trying to hold ourselves roughly to Classic power budgets for each class meant that every new element we added needed to come at the expense of something else. Those reductions left some iconic abilities feeling lackluster, and closed the door to other potentially exciting design options. So over the last two weeks, we've raised damage on classes across the game, and have increased the health of higher level creatures to compensate. This additional “headroom” has allowed us to tune things to a place that we hope feels better overall. Beyond that, some of this round of changes reflects areas where we were likely hasty in turning to Burning Crusade- or Wrath-era solutions rather than carving out new ones that better fit into the Forever combat model. Our aim in class design is not perfect numerical equality, but rather for every class to feel valuable to the groups they join, with powerful, unforgettable moments brought on by mastering them. In Forever this is accomplished by doubling down on the strengths and differences that make each class unique, rather than overly unifying them."

Developers' notes: "We've used the data and feedback gathered during Beta testing to get everything tuned to a reasonable place. However, the only true test of that tuning is the game itself. With the exception of bugs and serious outliers, we don't plan on making big tuning changes between now and the opening of the raids next month. Once we have sufficient data from players leveling past 30 and engaging in a wide range of content, we expect that we will do a large tuning pass based on our data. And this is all merely a starting point for the classes in Forever, which will continue to evolve over the course of the months and years ahead just as they did following the original launch in 2004."
Learning a new spell no longer puts it on your action bars.

Training costs are adjusted for every class: most abilities learned at the same level cost the same, and training everything from 1 to 60 now costs 206 to 207 gold (Warlocks less, to cover their pets' Grimoires).
Throw uses its 0.5 sec windup again (it was using the throwing weapon's attack speed).
Legacy Reward - Replica Ironforge Air Rifle works on allies who also have one equipped. Its quitter debuff lasts 40 sec (was 5 min) and its stun 2.5 sec (was 3).
Every race now has the right base stats; for example Tauren Warriors start with +5 Strength over Human Warriors (was +2). Skyborne got the same fix.
Roots from procs (Frostbite, Entrapment, Improved Wing Clip, Counterattack, Improved Hamstring) now have diminishing returns.
Darkspear Islands: dropping the flag no longer gives the dropper the "Recently Dropped Flag" debuff.
Gamepad support is in a functional beta: all major gameplay and the core interface work with a controller, customizable through Edit Mode and the Options menu.
Many fixes and improvements to the Gamepad action bars, bags, targeting, flight paths, pets, professions, quests and tooltips.
Bags no longer equip themselves into free bag slots.
Faster respawns in many areas for launch, fastest in the starting zones.

Developers' notes: "Our goal with these adjustments is to properly support large player volumes at launch, so that players aren't hitting hard bottlenecks and can continue to enjoy the game. Some contention for spawns is expected and part of the experience - it is not our goal to remove that. These adjusted rates are generally on the faster side in lower-level zones - with starting zones being the fastest - and gradually fall to slower rates as you level up, consistent with when players naturally spread out across the many zones available in WoW Forever. Once the initial launch surge of low-level characters has settled down, we will adjust the lower-level zones down to more typical rates."

Quest experience, prerequisites and levels adjusted; Ruins of Lordaeron dungeon quests now all start at level 15. Fixes in Alterac Mountains, the Barrens, Darkshore, Mulgore, Orgrimmar, Teldrassil and the Wetlands.
